execution.ref: OPERATOR-USABILITY-01 (.agent/decisions/2026-10-05-OPERATOR-USABILITY-01.md), branch claude/operator-usability; findings B2, B3, B8, B10 and C1 from the Graphite Test executor's Launchpad usability findings, 2026-10-05.
execution.description: Operator and agent usability fixes: the owner report carries the campaign controller's settled state and time, the halt operation's text names stop and pause, phase 3 reconcile says when an uncertain pod create settles, and phase 4 ends typed errors as typed refusals.

expected: An operator or agent can tell from Carbon's own outputs when a campaign has stopped running, how to stop it, when a reconcile can succeed, and why a phase-4 command refused.
observed: The report's completed_unix is written only for a finished finite campaign, so a READY campaign's report looked like it was still running; an existing stop tool was missed because it is called halt; reconcile exited 4 for up to 600 s with no time to retry; phase 4 ended controller and knowledge refusals in tracebacks; a short-lived MCP launch was left QUEUED for a reason the code alone could not show.
keep: One operation table generates both doors: make an existing operation easier to find instead of adding a second name for it.
A field that means 'finished' keeps one meaning; a different state such as settled or waiting for the miner gets its own field.
A refusal that will clear with time states the time, rounded up, not just the exit code.
change: Every derived report is rewritten when the state it summarizes changes, not only when the process that wrote it closes.
A stuck-state finding needs the run's records attached (dispatch rows, last_refusal, interruptions, process list) before the fix is chosen; without them the root cause stays open.
